source_gap: Existing source establishes voluntary offers of help and conditional acceptance of requested coordination, but not typical entry sequence into meaningful chosen group roles.
prompt: When you have an opportunity to help someone or take responsibility, what do you usually do? If you become responsible, does it tend to start with your offer, another person's request, something developing naturally, or does it depend? You might not take a role at all.
role_definition: Offering help, accepting a request, having something assigned, and gradually becoming involved are different experiences. Not participating is also an answer.

allowed_origins.label: I proposed, volunteered for, or began taking the role before anyone asked.
Another person specifically asked, invited, or appointed me before I proposed it.
It followed an existing obligation, rotation, job assignment or practical necessity.
We decided jointly; no clear first mover.
I offered help but did not actually take responsibility for a role.

overall_question: If you can identify a recurring pattern from actual situations, which is closest?

pattern_choices.label: I more often take the initiative, without waiting to be asked.
I more often take roles after someone independently asks or invites me.
Most roles arise from obligations, assignment or necessity.
Different contexts lead to different patterns; no single route dominates.
I cannot tell from my experience.
Another pattern — explain in the conditions field.

neutral_followup: Only if helpful: briefly describe one real situation or exception. No quota or required examples.
participant_scope: No natal features, astrology terms, intended scoring direction or respondent birth information appears in the questionnaire.
coding_rule: Never infer invited-entry from mere willingness to accept a request, or initiated-entry from offering help without responsibility. Do not infer long-term propensity from a single scenario, isolated event or prompted label. Preserve mixed, other, insufficient and context-dependent as non-scoring unless genuinely resolved.
followup_policy: Default is one short free-text response; do not request examples or a stable pattern after an adequate conditional answer. Optional detail remains available, up to three examples only if participant chooses to add them. Preserve previous V3.3 examples on import.
codebook_boundary: Development measurement only. The separate frozen V1.5 recognition_entry semantics are not modified or automatically populated. Do not treat this as a new independent validation of the known developer birth.
version_note: v1.1 UX repair; same stable V3.3 export schema with optional summary string
